# Project-authored Keynote literal-footer A/B controls

These exact archives are root's Keynote 15.1.1 exports of the MIT-licensed synthetic sixteen-slide Arial qualification fixture. The baseline generator is commit `4a3d32ea5fb870bbae574974f4e1c19dda00549b`; maintained one-variable control preparation is commit `42dddedab6b6309b2fc5ebd669fb4cdce670457a`. Source inputs A and B differ only in sixteen selected slide-local literal `ftr` binding tokens; all other uncompressed parts are exact. Root opened each fresh input, saved a separate Keynote document, exported PPTX and inspected reopens on 2026-10-15. `manifest.json` records input identities and exact retained output sizes/hashes. Never regenerate the fixtures to make a test pass.

Both outputs strip the literal's `ftr` role and customer tags, retain its exact generated name, own bottom-band frame and current words, and retain a unique same-group live slide-number placeholder on precisely the same row. A moves the literal behind K08's image; B retains its foreground ordering. That bounded native visibility result is separate from semantic import classification. The ordinary current literal must be recognized without reading an original source value; native literal brace tokens must remain literal on re-export.

The fixture contains project-authored text, notes and synthetic image/chart/table objects, with no font programs bundled. Tests run without native applications, machine fonts, transfers or network. This is not a published-graph, physical-font, raster/geometry or general native acceptance claim. Sixteen removed notes-page number fields and other explicit import adaptations remain separate findings.

`before-imports.json` contains the complete imports and nineteen diagnostics from clean PPTX main `7f300b42166c55ee14f8f9432e7340ded26f5ee4`, using this branch's unchanged frozen dependency installation. Its sealed hash is in the manifest. The test applies only the explicitly asserted sixteen literal-block removals and deck-footer addition, then compares the complete new document and diagnostics. It never supplies these old words or styles to the importer.
